field_patch.description_long: Time reported on August 17, 2016, that Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner spent a day aboard David Geffen’s yacht while vacationing in Croatia. Wendi Deng, Rupert Murdoch’s former wife, joined them. The contemporaneous story followed a photograph Ivanka had posted from Croatia and described a summer outing with the couple and Deng aboard Geffen’s yacht. A separate Croatian article, published years later, summarized an allegation of a meeting with an unnamed Russian oligarch during the trip, based on documents reported by BuzzFeed. The supplied record does not include those underlying interview documents or establish that the alleged meeting took place, and Time’s 2016 account does not report it. Deng’s personal relationships do not establish anything about the Trump family’s conduct. The documented event is the family members’ yacht outing with Deng. The available reporting identifies no political or legal consequence from that vacation and does not show Donald Trump joined the outing.

reason: Clarifies the allegation without implying that Donald Trump attended the alleged meeting; the source packet does not establish the meeting or identify its participants clearly enough to state them as fact.

field_patch.description_long: On April 29, 2019, President Donald Trump sent the Senate a message stating that he had concluded the United States should not become a party to the Arms Trade Treaty. The United States had signed the treaty but had not ratified it. The UN Treaty Collection records a U.S. communication received on July 18, 2019, saying that the country did not intend to become a party. The two official records document Trump’s stated decision and the later communication to the treaty depositary. They do not describe the United States leaving a treaty to which it had become a party through ratification. The account concerns ending the effort to join the treaty and withdrawing the U.S. signature. It does not establish later effects on arms transfers or other countries’ treaty participation. The decision ended the U.S. effort to join the treaty.

reason: Removes a source-review note about the unsupported convention announcement from the public copy while retaining the documented decision and meeting the long-description length requirement.

field_patch.title: U.S. Sent 238 Venezuelans to CECOT in 2025; HRW Reports Detention Concerns
field_patch.description_medium: Human Rights Watch reported that the United States removed 238 Venezuelans to El Salvador on March 15, 2025 and transferred them to CECOT. HRW interviewed relatives who could not obtain information about detainees’ locations and said authorities had not disclosed a legal basis for detention. HRW described the situation as enforced disappearance and arbitrary detention; these are its legal assessments, not a court ruling.

reason: Names the single cited rights organization and removes an imperative editorial instruction from the proposed description.
